subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack edit/delete subtype events remain session-scoped system events, or should OpenClaw add a documented opt-in Slack config field to drop selected subtypes before session wake?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the requested fix adds a public Slack config key and changes channel event policy, which repository policy treats as maintainer/product territory.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
options.body: Add `ignoreSubtypes` for selected Slack edit/delete subtypes, default to current behavior, and test that matching events are dropped before session context.

options.title: Change default policy
options.body: Stop queuing edit/delete system events by default, accepting the compatibility impact for users who currently use those metadata events as passive context.

options.title: Keep current system events
options.body: Decline the config key and document that Slack edit/delete metadata remains session-scoped system context with prompt or policy workarounds.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
recommendation.body: Add `ignoreSubtypes` for selected Slack edit/delete subtypes, default to current behavior, and test that matching events are dropped before session context.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on Slack subtype system-event policy and the adjacent thread-broadcast decision.
